newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-COOL MOYA ONE STEP FROM TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COOL MOYA ONE STEP FROM TITLE.

text.p: Spaniard Carlos Moya showed the tennis world on Thursday that he has the potential to be a champion.
Moya has gained plenty of admirers at the Australian Open since he beat defending champion Boris Becker in the first round.
But the unseeded Spaniard, who plays in a bandana and surf shorts, was not given much chance against world number two Michael Chang in Thursday's semifinals.
Moya proved the doubters wrong and overwhelmed Chang in straight sets to set up a possible final showdown with world number one Pete Sampras.
Even Chang, who never takes an opponent for granted, had not believed that the Spaniard, ranked 25th in the world, had the mettle to make it to the end of a grand slam.
"I was pretty much thinking what everybody else was thinking: he's played some good tennis coming in (to the tournament), but I don't think anyone expected him to come into the final," Chang said.

Moya is rapidly closing the gap between himself and the sport's elite. He has rocketed up the rankings in the past year, beating world number five Thomas Muster and world number four Goran Ivanisevic in the months leading up to the Australian Open. He also broke into the top 20 for the first time.
He has also helped shatter the belief that Spaniards only know their way around a clay court.
One of the few top players Moya has not beaten is Sampras, who plays fifth-seeded Muster in the other semifinal on Friday.
Moya said of a possible clash with Sampras, eight times a grand slam tournament winner, on Sunday: "He's number one, but I beat number two and number six. I'm not going on court a loser."

Moya has met Sampras once before in his short career. Ranked 315 at the time, he played a tiebreak against Sampras at a tennis clinic in Barcelona two years ago. "He beat me, I was nervous. Now things have changed."
Raised on the resort island of Mallorca, rock and roll fan Moya now lives in Barcelona and is as relaxed as his background suggests.
"Now I have beaten Becker I have a different look, a different way of playing tennis maybe," he said.
"I know the crowd like it because they support me a lot. They support me in the bad moments when I'm going down."
